comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimensions must be provided to verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained from all buildings to existing overhead electric conductors.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8 on site plan

comment: Plans must show radial clearance dimensions from the outside conductor of overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors to all proposed buildings, parking areas, and site facilities, demonstrating minimum 15-foot radial clearance is maintained.
applicableAreas: All proposed buildings and site facilities

comment: Building elevation drawings must show all building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, patios) with clearance dimensions to overhead electric conductors demonstrating both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances are maintained.
applicableAreas: All proposed buildings

comment: Section views and plan dimensions must demonstrate that elevated walkways and platforms maintain minimum 15-foot radial clearance from the outside conductor of overhead distribution facilities.
applicableAreas: Elevated walkways and stairs shown on site plan

comment: Building elevation sheets must show surveyed overhead conductor elevations with clearance dimensions demonstrating buildings maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from electric facilities in adjacent right-of-way.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1, 2, and other structures near Valley View Road right-of-way

comment: Building elevation sheets showing surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors with clearance dimension annotations must be provided to demonstrate required clearances are met. These sheets must be sealed by a registered surveyor and engineer.
applicableAreas: All proposed buildings

comment: Section and plan view exhibits with dimension lines from the outer conductor to the outermost edge of buildings and building projections must be provided for all proposed structures within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: All buildings and projections

comment: Plan dimensions must show fence alignments maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor (not from pole centerline) of existing overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Fence perimeter as shown on site plan

comment: Plan view dimensions must demonstrate fence post locations maintain minimum 10-foot horizontal clearance from existing electric utility pole centers.
applicableAreas: Fencing locations relative to existing utility poles

comment: Plan and section views must show dimensions from the outermost electric line to retaining wall faces, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls around site perimeter

comment: Section exhibits must show dimensions from the outer conductor to the outermost edge of each retaining wall for clearance verification.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls

comment: Grading plan and section views must show vertical clearance dimensions from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities (including telecommunications attachments) to finished driveway grade, demonstrating 16-foot minimum (18-foot if truck traffic).
applicableAreas: All driveways on site

comment: Plans must clearly indicate whether existing electric poles conflict with proposed driveway alignments. If conflicts exist, relocation notes or revised pole locations must be shown with minimum 30-foot separation from driveway edge.
applicableAreas: Driveway alignments

comment: Any clearance dimension annotations must explicitly show that dimensions are measured from the outside conductor (the actual electric wire), not from utility pole centerline. Dimension lines must originate at the outer conductor location.
applicableAreas: All clearance dimensions shown on plans

comment: Plan view must clarify that new or modified sidewalks at each end of the property along right-of-way frontage are cleared of existing power poles, or if poles must be relocated to accommodate sidewalk.
applicableAreas: Sidewalk alignments at property boundaries along Valley View Road

comment: Utility plan must show clearance dimensions from water meter locations to existing overhead electric service drop conductors, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance.
applicableAreas: Water meter locations shown on utility plan

comment: Utility plan must show clearance dimensions between proposed water line routing and existing overhead distribution poles and conductors.
applicableAreas: Water line routing on utility plans

comment: Plans must verify that permanent structure foundations within 5 feet of property line allow adequate clearance space (typically 5-7 feet from property line) for installation and maintenance of electric facilities in adjacent ROW or easement areas.
applicableAreas: Foundations within 5 feet of property line

comment: Registered surveyor clearance survey showing pole locations and mid-span clearances from overhead facilities to driveways, parking areas, and buildings must be provided to verify all vertical clearance requirements (7.5-foot, 16-foot, 18-foot) are satisfied.
applicableAreas: All areas where overhead facilities may affect site features

comment: Photometric plan or site plan must show decorative lighting fixture locations with clearance verification demonstrating 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from overhead lines, or relocation notes if conflicts exist.
applicableAreas: Proposed decorative lighting locations

comment: Landscape plan must verify that all trees proposed within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors or 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors (per more restrictive UCM 50-foot standard) are species marked 'UC' (Utility Compatible) in ECM Appendix F, generally mature height ≤20 feet. Annotate lateral distances.
applicableAreas: Proposed tree plantings on landscape plan

comment: Electrical plan details must verify that meter access areas maintain required working clearances: 30-inch-wide clear space, 36-inch front depth, 6.5-foot headroom, with no obstructions from fences, walls, equipment, vegetation, or building projections.
applicableAreas: Proposed electric meter locations

comment: Site plan must clearly document clearances from proposed buildings and structures to existing streetlight pole locations.
applicableAreas: Proposed buildings in relation to existing streetlights

comment: Site plan must show down guy wire anchor locations from existing poles and verify they do not conflict with proposed accessible paths or driveways. If conflicts exist, plans must show pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting steel poles.
applicableAreas: Accessible paths and driveway alignments

comment: Easement exhibit must show dedicated easements for any down guy anchors from existing distribution poles, 10 feet wide extending minimum 5 feet past where anchor enters ground.
applicableAreas: Down guy anchor locations

comment: Electrical plan section views must show vertical clearance dimensions from overhead line conductors to the top of all transformer equipment, demonstrating 7.5-foot minimum sky-to-ground clearance.
applicableAreas: Proposed transformer pad locations

comment: Site logistics or construction phasing plan must show construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, and work platform locations with verified 10-foot radial clearance from overhead electric lines per OSHA and Texas law requirements.
applicableAreas: Construction staging areas

comment: Plans must include a note stating: 'Owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines' per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.
applicableAreas: Cover sheet or general notes

comment: Non-utility-compatible trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak) are positioned along the overhead electric distribution line boundary on the landscape plan without documented clearance verification or Austin Energy written approval. Provide documented Austin Energy approval authorizing these species within the restricted zone, or relocate trees to beyond 15 lateral feet from the outside conductor.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where OHE distribution line runs

comment: Large trees (Cedar Elm at 40-50 feet, Live Oak at 50-80 feet, Hackberry at 40-60 feet mature height) are positioned along the overhead electric distribution line without documented clearance verification or Austin Energy approval. Provide clearance calculations or documented Austin Energy approval for trees within 25 feet of the distribution conductor, or relocate large trees to beyond 25 lateral feet from the outside conductor.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where OHE distribution line runs

comment: Trees are positioned along the OHE line boundary where utility poles are located. Provide clearance documentation demonstrating all trees are at least 10 lateral feet from each pole, or relocate trees to meet this clearance requirement.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where utility poles are located

comment: Underground electric equipment locations from electrical plan (Sheet 21) are not shown on landscape plan (Sheet 31). Provide landscape plan with underground equipment (pull boxes, vaults) overlaid and labeled, with clearance dimensions from proposed and retained trees to all underground equipment, or add dimension callouts demonstrating trees are at least 5 lateral feet from all underground equipment.
applicableAreas: Locations of underground electric pull boxes and vaults

comment: For any trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment, provide root barrier details on a landscape detail sheet specifying minimum 4-foot depth and 5-foot offset from equipment. Alternatively, provide landsca plan documentation showing all trees are beyond 20 feet from underground equipment.
applicableAreas: Trees within 20 feet of underground electric equipment

comment: Large trees (mature height ≥40 feet) are not differentiated on the landscape plan. Add a note to the plant schedule specifying mature height for each proposed tree species, and use a distinct symbol or notation on the landscape plan to identify large trees (Cedar Elm ~40-50 ft, Live Oak ~50-80 ft, Hackberry ~40-60 ft) to allow verification of electrical clearance compliance.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan where trees are proposed near overhead electric facilities

comment: Trees are positioned within prohibited electrical clearance zones without documented written approval from Austin Energy. Obtain and submit explicit written approval from Austin Energy authorizing the proposed tree placement (species, locations, and sizes) within restricted zones, or relocate all trees to comply with minimum clearance distances (15 feet from distribution conductors for non-utility-compatible trees, 25 feet for large trees, 10 feet from utility poles).
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where trees are positioned near OHE line and poles

comment: Transformer pads shown on electrical plan but without any documented clearance measurements or dimension callouts to verify 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance from buildings, structures, and foundations. Applicant must provide dimensioned site plan or construction details showing clearances from each pad to adjacent structures.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pads 1, 2, 3, 4 on electrical design plan (Sheet 21)

comment: Transformer Pad 4 is positioned very close to the southern property line wood fence with no documented clearance measurements. Applicant must provide dimensioned clearances from the pad to the adjacent fence, and clarify the access door orientation to determine whether 5-foot clearance (if operators/controls side) or 3-foot clearance (if non-access side) applies. If clearance is less than required, additional setback or fence modification must be documented.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 4 (southern property line, adjacent to wood fence)

comment: If any transformer pads are proposed with clearances less than 5 feet to brick or masonry buildings, the plans must include documentation of: (1) written Austin Energy Design approval, (2) verification of minimum 3-hour fire rating in the clearance area (from architectural specifications), (3) confirmation that the location is not in a confined space, (4) verification of minimum 10 feet clearance to windows/doors/ducts, and (5) verification of minimum 15 feet vertical clearance to windows/doors/ducts. No such documentation is currently provided.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads shown on Sheet 21

comment: If balconies or overhangs exist on adjacent buildings within 5 feet of any transformer pads, provide building elevation views confirming minimum 5-foot lateral clearance and verification that no coverings or structures exist directly above pad or minimum equipment area.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (Sheet 21)

comment: Applicant must provide building elevations and electrical equipment specifications (oil-filled vs. dry-type) for each transformer. If windows, doors, or ventilating ducts exist on adjacent buildings, provide dimensioned clearances showing minimum 12-foot horizontal clearance from edge of oil-filled equipment pad when window/door/duct is less than 12 feet from grade or has less than 5 feet lateral separation.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if windows/doors/ducts are adjacent)

comment: Sidewalk is shown adjacent to Transformer Pad 1 on Site Plan (Sheet 9) without documented clearance dimension. Applicant must provide measured distance from transformer pad edge to back of sidewalk, confirming minimum 2-foot clearance.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 1 (western entrance area, adjacent to sidewalk)

comment: If exterior stairwells serving as fire exits exist adjacent to any transformer pads, provide site plan showing stairwell locations and documented clearances from pads.

If fire escapes or stairs serving as fire exits exist on adjacent buildings, provide site plan with dimensioned locations showing minimum 20-foot horizontal/radial clearance from edge of oil-filled transformer pad. Provide electrical specifications identifying equipment as oil-filled.

Applicant must clearly identify the access door orientation (with directional arrow or note) for each transformer pad on the electrical plan, and provide dimensioned measurements from the access door side of each pad to the nearest open area or adjacent building/structure, confirming minimum 10-foot clearance in the hot-stick use area.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (Pads 1, 2, 3, 4 on Sheet 21)

comment: If any transformer locations involve niches (equipment accessible from outside but within building footprint) or enclosed/notched-out building configurations, provide cross-section drawings demonstrating minimum 35-foot vertical clearance from grade through entire access path, and provide documentation of 3-hour fire wall rating and ventilation specifications.
Provide dimensioned measurements on electrical plan showing minimum 5-foot clearance from each transformer pad to fire hydrant locations identified on the fire protection plan (Sheet 10).
applicableAreas: All transformer pads relative to fire hydrant locations (Sheet 21 vs. Sheet 10)

comment: Applicant must provide a utility compatibility analysis documenting: (1) which trees are located within 10 lateral feet of each transformer pad or 15 lateral feet of overhead distribution, (2) confirmation that all such trees are identified as utility-compatible species per ECM Appendix F 'UC' column, with species names and caliper information. If non-compatible species are within these proximity ranges, relocation or removal must be shown.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) relative to transformer locations (Sheet 21)

comment: Applicant must: (1) clearly identify access door orientation on each transformer pad on the electrical plan, (2) provide detailed landscape plan analysis showing minimum 10-foot clearance from transformer access door sides and minimum 5-foot clearance from non-access sides for all shrubs, groundcovers, and low-lying vegetation, with specific plant types and locations dimensioned.
applicableAreas: Landscape planting areas (Sheet 31) relative to transformer locations (Sheet 21)

comment: Applicant must identify all trees on landscape plan (Sheet 31) that are located within 20 lateral feet of transformer pad locations (Sheet 21), and provide detailed root barrier specifications showing minimum 4-foot depth installed 5 feet from equipment edge. Include root barrier details on landscape detail sheet (Sheet 37) with cross-references to specific tree locations.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) relative to transformer locations (Sheet 21)

comment: If dumpsters or trash collection enclosures are provided on site, identify their locations on site plan with dimensioned clearances showing minimum 5-foot distance from each transformer pad.

Identify bike rack locations on site plan with dimensioned clearances showing minimum 5-foot distance from each transformer pad. Sheet 22 notes 3-foot utility clearance standard for racks; ensure this is met in relation to transformer locations.
If light poles are located adjacent to transformer pads, provide site plan with dimensioned clearances showing minimum 5-foot distance from each pad.

Transformer Pad 4 is located in the south-central area corresponding to the designated fire lane. Provide dimensioned clearance on electrical plan showing minimum 15-foot distance from transformer pad edge to fire lane centerline. If clearance is inadequate, relocate pad to satisfy fire lane requirements.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 4 (southern area near fire lane)

comment: Provide utility coordination drawing or table showing minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to water service lines. Dimensions on electrical plan must verify clearances from all pad edges to nearest water utility.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (Sheet 21) relative to water utility routing (Sheet 19)

comment: Provide utility coordination drawing or table showing minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to wastewater service lines and cleanouts. Dimensions on electrical plan must verify clearances from all pad edges to nearest wastewater utility.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (Sheet 21) relative to wastewater utility routing (Sheet 19)

comment: Provide utility coordination showing minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from each transformer pad to storm drain lines. Cross-reference electrical plan with storm sewer plan (Sheet 12) with dimensions verifying all clearances.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (Sheet 21) relative to storm drain routing (Sheet 12)

comment: If gas service is provided, confirm the presence of gas lines on utility plans and provide minimum horizontal clearance dimensions (24 inches for gas pipelines less than 60 psi, 36 inches for high-pressure gas 60 psi and over) from transformer pads.

Provide comprehensive utility coordination table or drawing showing horizontal and vertical separation from each transformer pad to all underground utilities including telecom, cable, reclaimed water (if present), and any other utilities not specifically covered under the 5-foot water/wastewater/storm drain requirements. Minimum 12-inch clearance (OD to OD) must be documented.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads relative to all underground utilities

comment: Provide utility coordination analysis confirming: (1) transformer pads and AE underground facilities do not cross under/over other utility lines, (2) no customer buildings, foundations, or structures (including footings) are located over or immediately adjacent to AE underground electrical facilities, and (3) adequate vertical separation is maintained between all utilities.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads and underground electrical routing relative to other utilities

comment: If overhead distribution lines exist on adjacent properties or streets near transformer pad locations, provide site plan with dimensioned horizontal sky-to-ground clearances (minimum 7.5 feet) extending from ground to sky above all transformer pads and proposed structures.

If overhead distribution primary or neutral conductors are present on adjacent properties, provide site plan with dimensioned radii (minimum 15 feet measured from conductor centerline, not pole centerline) showing clearance from all transformer pad locations and proposed structures to overhead conductors.

Provide cross-section drawings at typical transformer pad locations showing vertical clearances from ground grade to any overhead structures, roofs, overhangs, utility lines, or other obstructions. Cross-sections should be at least at two locations representing the site's varied topography. Verify clearances meet UCM § 1.10.3 requirements.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations with potential overhead structures

comment: Applicant must: (1) specify on electrical plan whether each transformer is oil-filled or dry-type, (2) for oil-filled equipment, provide grading plan with drainage arrows and slope percentages at each pad location confirming liquid flow is directed away from buildings and adjacent structures, and (3) confirm minimum 1% slope away from all pad locations.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads relative to grading on Sheet 11

comment: Provide explicit notation or dimension table on electrical plan confirming: (1) each transformer pad is located 100% on private property (with distance from property boundary), (2) no pad is located in public right-of-way, and (3) no pad straddles a property line. Cross-reference property boundaries from plat (Sheet 2) with pad locations on electrical plan (Sheet 21).
applicableAreas: All transformer pads shown on Sheet 21

comment: Provide easement compliance analysis confirming: (1) each transformer pad location relative to recorded easements (drainage, water, sewer, overhead electric), (2) if any pad is located within a prohibited easement, provide written Austin Energy Design approval, or (3) revise plans to locate all pads outside easement boundaries. Reference recorded easement instrument numbers and provide cross-referenced site plan showing easement boundaries overlaid with transformer pad locations.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads relative to recorded easements on property

comment: Applicant must: (1) coordinate with Austin Energy Design to determine the required transformer easement width for each pad, (2) depict transformer easement boundaries (not just note 'additional easements may be required') on the site plan and electrical plan, (3) document easement width in plan notes, and (4) ensure easement boundaries are not in conflict with recorded property easements or other site features.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads shown on Sheet 21

comment: Provide notation on electrical plan confirming that 100% of electrical routing from each transformer pad to its associated meter(s) is located on private property, with no portion in public right-of-way. Include cross-reference to property boundaries from site plan (Sheet 9) and plat (Sheet 2).
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from all transformer pads to associated meters

comment: Applicant must: (1) obtain Austin Energy Design approval documents and transformer pad detail sheets for each of the 4 transformer pads, (2) confirm the service type (single-phase or three-phase) for each pad and the associated electrical load, (3) depict the AE Design-approved pad dimensions (length × width) on the electrical plan for each pad, and (4) provide the approved detail sheets as part of the plan set (reference from electrical plan detail callouts).
applicableAreas: All transformer pads shown on Sheet 21

comment: Applicant must: (1) provide dimensioned measurements on electrical plan showing distance from each transformer pad to nearest parking stall or vehicle circulation route, (2) for any pad within 4 feet of parking/circulation areas, provide bollard details referencing AE Design equipment pad specifications showing: 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts, spacing that allows equipment door opening, and installation details, or (3) if no bollards are required, document that all pads are more than 4 feet from parking/vehicle areas.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads relative to parking areas and drive lanes

comment: If overhead distribution facilities exist on adjacent properties or streets, confirm through site plan and utility notes that no customer buildings, parking garages, structures, poles, signs, antennas, tanks, or other facilities are installed under or over overhead distribution primary or neutral conductors.
